diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Script body in proposal: ~328 lines (vs 142 pre-refactor). Justified because the 6-record dispatch table (5 fields × 4 atomic targets + 2 aggregate-target expansions = 22 variable assignments) plus per-target conditional code paths (binary check function, docker union compute, PID verify loop, session save case, detached-kill case) cannot fit in the no-arg-only single-flow shape of the pre-refactor script. The original 142-line shape only handled one fixed target set (3 prod daemons + Docker); supporting 6 targets with per-target lock, binary gate, save/kill/Docker/start/verify pathways inherently requires a dispatch table + helper functions. Each line beyond the budget is justified by an AC requirement (AC1 dispatch table, AC2 per-target binary glob, AC3 conditional Docker, AC6 per-target save, AC7 per-target verify, AC8 fail-closed unknown target, S1 per-target detached-kill, S2 per-target flock, S4 audit-tag log function). Note: diff_stats files_changed=0 because the proposal was NOT applied to /root/bin/happy-restart.sh (hook-blocked); user must apply manually from TTY.

implementation_notes: The proposal markdown is the deliverable, NOT the on-disk /root/bin/happy-restart.sh. C3's hook hardening (which is now LIVE) blocks all subagent Edit/Write to that path. This is the runtime enforcement of the C1-after-C3 sequencing constraint. User must apply manually from TTY.

The proposal preserves the `happy-restart` substring in the post-apply filename so /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-bash-safety.sh:345 continues to fire and Claude remains permanently blocked from invoking the script. This is documented in the proposal header at line ~165 of the script body.

Aggregate-target paths (all-prod / all) deliberately use VERBATIM pre-refactor code blocks for save (line 299) and detached-kill loop (lines 354-365). This is the AC4 regression-guard mechanism: byte-for-byte preservation of today's behavior when no --target arg is supplied (which dispatches through all-prod).

AC2 E3 'fail-fast prevents half-restart': the binary gate runs at step 5 (lines 423-447 in proposal), AFTER the daemon-stop step 2 (lines 311-315) but BEFORE the Docker recreate step 6 (lines 461-475) and BEFORE the daemon-start step 7 (lines 481-487). This matches the pre-refactor ordering (gate at lines 51-88, between stop at 22-26 and Docker at 90-93). To fully fail-fast BEFORE any stop, the gate would need to move to step 1 — but that breaks AC4 byte-for-byte preservation. Documented as intentional trade-off in proposal AC E3 row.

OBJ-C1-002 (worktree dist authoring-time content): proposal markdown documents in script body comment at lines 161-165 the expectation that /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/packages/happy-cli/dist/ contains >=2 .mjs files. The fail-closed binary gate handles the empty-dist case correctly via FIX hint pointing at `cd /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/packages/happy-cli && yarn build`.

Lockfile path /var/run/happy-restart-${TARGET}.lock falls back to /tmp if /var/run is not writable (line 257-259). Each target has its own lockfile so concurrent restarts of different stacks don't block each other, but `--target dev` twice serializes correctly.

The proposal's static-inspection AC verification matrix (lines 39-72 of proposal markdown) gives QA close-cycle a self-contained set of grep patterns to run, eliminating the PASS_AS_SUBSTITUTE anti-pattern QA flagged in OBJ-C1-001. QA's runtime MEASURABLE clauses (AC2 docker ps CreatedAt, AC5 grep TASK-ID /var/log, AC8 echo $?) remain as user-from-TTY post-apply verifications, but the static parallels make subagent close-cycle possible without runtime.
